client.name: T Wireless
client.address: 965 Bovaird Dr W, Unit 1, Brampton, ON

form.title: T Wireless website: quick questions
form.description:
Hi Ali,

We’re building the new T Wireless website. We want it to say only what’s true about your store, so we need your help with a few facts.

Most questions are one tap. If you’re not sure, choose “Not sure” and we’ll work it out together. Nothing goes on the website until you’ve seen it and said yes.

There are three parts. Part 1 (about 10 minutes) is what we need first. Parts 2 and 3 are shorter, and you can stop at the end of any part.

Prepared by EMBLEM-NLP.
form.confirmation:
Thank you, Ali. We’ll update the draft with your answers and send it back for you to check. Nothing goes on the website until you say yes.

If you stopped early, use “Edit your response” below to carry on whenever you like.

parts.title: Part 1 of 3: What we need first
parts.required_for: the first new pages (phones, repairs, business) and the web address

parts.title: Part 2 of 3: Before the site goes live
parts.required_for: the statements the site makes about how the store works

parts.title: Part 3 of 3: For the next pages
parts.required_for: trade-ins, accessories, about the store, repair terms, accessibility and social links

sections.title: Part 1 of 3: About you
sections.description: This part is what we need first. It takes about 10 minutes.

questions.title: Your name
Which best describes you?
options: I own the store and decide about the website
I own the store with a partner or family member, and we decide together
I manage the store and need the owner’s OK
questions.why: Tells us who can approve what the site claims.

questions.title: What’s the best way to reach you with a quick question?

sections.title: Your store’s details
sections.description: We have these from your business card, Google and Bell’s store finder. Please tell us which ones are right.

questions.title: Which postal code is right for 965 Bovaird Dr W, Unit 1?
questions.help: Your business card and Google show L6X 0G3 (the card reads “I6X OG3”). Bell’s store finder, and MapQuest, show L6X 5K7. If neither is right, choose Other and type it.
questions.why: Two postal codes are in use online. A wrong one breaks the map pin, the Google listing match and the privacy page.

questions.title: Is 647-707-1093 the number customers should call?
questions.help: Not right? Choose Other and type the right number.

questions.title: Which email should customers see on the website?
questions.help: Want a different one? Choose Other and type it.
options: None. Customers should use the contact form

questions.title: What are your regular opening hours?
questions.help:
We found four different versions, so we want yours.
Bell: every day, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Google: Sunday 10:30 a.m. to 7 p.m., other days 10 to 8.
Yellow Pages: Monday to Friday 10 to 8, Saturday 11 to 6, Sunday 11 to 5.
MapQuest: Monday to Saturday 11 to 8, closed Sunday.
If none is right, choose Other and write your hours day by day.
options: Monday to Saturday 10 to 8, Sunday 10:30 to 7 (Google)
Monday to Friday 10 to 8, Saturday 11 to 6, Sunday 11 to 5 (Yellow Pages)
Monday to Saturday 11 to 8, closed Sunday (MapQuest)
questions.why: Four public sources disagree. The site’s open and closed signs follow whatever we put in the weekly hours.

questions.title: What should the website say about public holidays?
questions.help: Our draft tells visitors to phone first on a public holiday.
options: Keep that: phone first on public holidays
We’re open our usual hours on public holidays

questions.title: Google says your entrance is wheelchair accessible. Is that right?
options: Partly. A customer may need help or a door button

questions.title: Our map says: “South side of Bovaird, just east of Chinguacousy Rd.” Is that right?
questions.help: If not, choose Other and tell us how you’d describe where the store is.

sections.title: Your web address and online accounts
sections.description:
We looked up what exists online for T Wireless on October 28, 2026.

• twireless.ca and t-wireless.ca are not registered, so they’re free to claim.
• t-wireless.com is registered (since July 2024) and shows a “coming soon” page. We can’t see who owns it.
• twireless.com is registered and for sale through a broker.

We can’t see inside your Google or Facebook accounts, so these questions are about what you have.

questions.title: Does the store have a website today?
questions.help: If yes, choose Other and type the address.

questions.title: Who owns t-wireless.com, the “coming soon” page?
options: A family member, partner or friend does
A web designer or company set it up for us
questions.why: Registered July 29, 2024 through Squarespace Domains, served by Squarespace, with Mailgun mail records. The registrant is hidden, so only Ali can tell us whose it is.

questions.title: MapQuest lists tboothwireless.ca for your address. That’s tbooth wireless, a Canadian phone retailer. Is it connected to your store?
options: Yes, we are or were connected to them
questions.why: MapQuest’s description of this address (Apple, Samsung and Motorola phones; Rogers, Bell and Fido plans; trade-ins and recycling) says it was generated from the tbooth site.

questions.title: Which web address would you like for the new site?
questions.help: We suggest a .ca address. It tells customers you’re a Canadian business, and it costs a small yearly fee.
options: t-wireless.com, if it turns out to be ours

questions.title: Who manages your Google listing (Google Business Profile)?
questions.help: Search “T Wireless Brampton” on Google while signed in. If you see “Edit your profile”, you manage it.
options: I do, and I can sign in
questions.why: Ownership of a Google Business Profile isn’t visible from outside. Hours, the postal code and the rating all live there.

questions.title: Google shows 4.1 stars from 95 reviews. Can the website show your rating?
questions.help: It would link to your Google reviews.

questions.title: Is facebook.com/Ifix4uu the store’s Facebook page?
questions.help: Yellow Pages lists it as the store’s website.
options: It’s linked to the store but someone else runs it

questions.title: If someone else set up a website, Google listing, Facebook page or email for the store, who was it?
questions.help: Names or companies, and what they did. We’d also like to know where your web address and email were bought, for example Squarespace, Google or GoDaddy.

sections.title: What you sell and set up
sections.description: This is for the new “In store now” phones section and the services pages.

questions.title: Which phone brands do you usually have in the store?
questions.help: Yellow Pages lists iPhone, Android and HTC.

questions.title: Which of these do you sell?
questions.help: Yellow Pages says you sell new phones for all carriers and unlock phones.
options: Unlocked phones that work with any carrier

questions.title: How should the website talk about the phones you have?
questions.help: Stock changes every day, so we won’t call a model “in stock” unless you tell us to.
options: Show the brands we carry and ask people to call or text to check stock
Show a short list of current models. I’ll tell you when it changes

questions.title: Which of these can the store set up for a customer?
questions.help: Bell lists your store for mobile devices for business and consumers, and for home internet, TV and phone.
rows: Bell phones and plans
Virgin Plus phones and plans
Lucky Mobile phones and plans
Prepaid plans
Bell home internet
Fibe TV
Satellite TV
Bell Home Phone
Business mobile plans
Bell SmartPay (paying for a phone over time)
Device Return Option (also called Flex Option)
Phone unlocking

questions.title: Does the store repair devices?
options: Yes, but we send some repairs away

questions.title: Which brands do you repair?
questions.help: We’ll list these on the website.

questions.title: Which repairs do you do?
questions.help: Our draft lists screens, batteries, charging faults, cameras, speakers and microphones, and water damage.

questions.title: Do you quote the price before you start a repair?

sections.title: Business customers
sections.description: Bell lists your store for mobile devices for business customers. We’d like to add a Business page with a “Buying for a team?” button.

questions.title: Does the store help businesses and teams?
options: No, we focus on individuals and families

questions.title: How can you help a business?
options: Moving a team’s numbers from another provider
Paying for team phones over time (Bell SmartPay for business)
One person to call about the account

questions.title: What should a business have ready when it comes to you?
questions.help: Our draft says: how many phones it needs, the company’s details and, if it’s moving numbers, a recent bill from its current provider. Tick what you really ask for.
options: A recent bill from its current provider (to move numbers)
Photo ID for the person who signs

questions.title: How should a business get in touch?
questions.help: This sets what the “Buying for a team?” button does.
options: Fill in a form on the website

sections.title: Part 1 is done. Thank you.
sections.description: Parts 2 and 3 are shorter. You can carry on now or come back later. If you stop here, use “Edit your response” on the next page to come back.

questions.title: What would you like to do?
options: I’ll finish later. Send what I’ve done so far

sections.title: Part 2 of 3: How the store works
sections.description: This part is what must be true before the site goes live. It takes about 6 minutes. Our draft pages describe how a visit goes. Tell us what’s true for your store.

questions.title: Which of these are true for your store?
questions.help: These are lines from our draft pages.
rows: For a repair, we give the customer a time to collect the phone.
When someone moves their number to us, we handle it and their old plan closes by itself.
We take trade-ins and tell the customer if their old phone can earn credit toward a new one.
We look up the customer’s address and book the Bell technician for home internet and TV.
We carry both iPhone and Android phones.
We can set up a plan on a phone the customer already owns.
If a customer rings first, we tell them whether a model or colour is in the store.
If a customer brings a recent bill, we go through offers, plans and home services with them.
Walk-ins are welcome and need no appointment.
If someone books a visit, we expect them.
Our staff call customers back after a form request.

questions.title: May we name you on the Visit page as the person to ask for?
questions.help: To use a different name, choose Other and type it.

questions.title: What do customers need to bring?
questions.help: Our draft says: photo ID in case it’s needed; a recent bill showing the account number when moving a number; the address with its unit number for home internet and TV; the phone for a repair. Tick what you really ask for.
options: A recent bill with the account number (to move a number)
The address with its unit number (home internet and TV)

questions.title: What should the website say about offers?
questions.help: Offers change often, so an old one on the website can cause problems at the counter.
options: Link to Bell’s offers page and keep the store’s own offers off the website
The store has its own offers. We’ll send you the details and end dates
No offers on the website for now

questions.title: Are these two lines on our draft pages still right?
rows: Virgin Plus prepaid plans end on January 15, 2027.
Virgin Plus hasn’t taken new home internet or TV customers in Ontario since January 14, 2026.

sections.title: Bell’s name and logos
sections.description: We want to follow Bell’s rules for dealers.

questions.title: How does Bell write your title on your dealer agreement or shop sign?
questions.help: Your card says “Authorised”. The decals in your window say “Authorized”.

questions.title: Has Bell said you can show the Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile logos on your website?
options: Yes, in writing or in a dealer kit

questions.title: Can the store show the Apple, Samsung and Google logos on its website?
questions.help: The draft puts each phone maker’s logo above its name on the Home, Phones and Repairs pages. The rules we found from Apple, Samsung and Google don’t mention Bell dealers. Tell us if Bell’s dealer kit or the maker says you can.
options: Yes, in writing or in a dealer kit
No, we were told not to

questions.title: Does Bell need to see or approve the website before it goes live?
Who is your Bell contact for dealer questions?
questions.help: A name, and a phone number or email. We’d like to check the program details (SmartPay, Device Return Option, and the Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile terms) with them.

questions.title: When someone sends a repair or visit request from the website, where should it go?
questions.help: To use a different email, choose Other and type it.

questions.title: What can the website promise about replies?
options: Nothing specific. Just say we’ll get back to them
We reply by the next business day
We reply within an hour while we’re open

questions.title: Who should customers contact about their personal information?
questions.help: A name and an email. Canadian privacy rules expect a named person.

questions.title: Our draft privacy page says you delete a request once you’re done with it, and show or erase what you hold if someone asks. Is that how you work?
options: Not exactly. I’ll explain at the end

questions.title: What should we do about photos?
questions.help: Real photos of the shop front, the counter and the repair bench look best.
options: I’ll send photos of the inside, the outside and the counter
I’d like help getting good photos

questions.title: May staff appear in photos?

sections.title: Part 2 is done. Thank you.
sections.description: Part 3 is optional. It covers trade-ins, accessories, your story and your social accounts. If you stop here, use “Edit your response” on the next page to come back.

questions.title: What would you like to do?
options: That’s enough for now. Send my answers

sections.title: Part 3 of 3: Trade-ins
sections.description: This part is optional. It helps with the next pages and takes about 8 minutes. One listing mentions trade-ins and recycling for your address, but its text came from a different company’s website, so we don’t want to guess.

questions.title: Do you take trade-ins?
options: Yes, the store pays its own cash or credit

questions.title: Which devices can people trade in?
How does the customer get the value of the old device?
options: Credit on a new phone or on the bill

questions.title: Does the store collect old devices for recycling?
Where do the collected devices go?
questions.help: For example a recycling program, Bell or a company. Leave blank if you’re not sure.

questions.title: Which accessories do you sell?
Do you fit screen protectors in the store?
Which payment methods do you accept?
Which of these can we say about the store?
questions.help: We’ll only say what you tick.
options: It’s an independent store, not owned by Bell
The owner is usually in the store

questions.title: In what year did the store open?
questions.help: Leave blank if you’d rather not say.

questions.title: Which languages can your team help customers in?
When can customers get help in those languages?
options: Only when certain staff are in

questions.title: What would you like customers to know about the store?
questions.help: For example why you opened, how long you’ve been in Brampton, or what you’re proud of.

questions.title: Would you like to introduce your team?
questions.help: Names and roles, one per line. Leave blank to skip.

questions.title: Do you give a warranty on repairs?
What isn’t covered by the warranty?
questions.help: For example new drops or water damage.

questions.title: What kind of parts do you use?
options: Original parts when we can get them

questions.title: If a customer doesn’t go ahead after you look at the phone, is there a charge?
How long does a typical screen repair take?
options: It depends. We quote when we see the phone

questions.title: Which of these does the store have?
questions.help: We’ll only list what you tick.
options: An automatic door or door button
Aisles wide enough for a wheelchair or scooter
A counter at a comfortable height for someone seated
Staff who will come to the door to help

questions.title: Who should customers contact if they need help using the store or the website?
options: The store’s usual phone and email

questions.title: Which social accounts does the store use?
Paste the links or names for each one.
Who posts on them?
How do customers get in touch today?
What would make the new website a success for you?
questions.help: Choose up to two.
options: People finding the store on Google

questions.title: Anything else we should know, or anything you definitely want or don’t want on the website?
